mcacapitals.dialogue.relaxed.response.ev: I thought so too, till he came round twice.
I was nowhere near it, and I'll swear that to a priest.
%122$s more days of black cloth, then back to business, I'd wager.
%50$s, and can't even manage a quiet exit. Says something, that.
I heard nothing, I saw nothing. Wise men do the same.
Wouldn't you hide too, with %20$s mouths in that household all wanting something from you?
%37$s doesn't answer to the likes of us. Never has.
Depends which lie you heard first.
Half of it's true and the other half's worse, knowing this village.
New writs mean new ways to fine a man for breathing wrong.
%64$s hasn't done an honest day's work since %145$s got the office, if you ask me.
More lords, more mouths, less bread for the rest of us.
%121$s knights to guard them and none to guard us.
Tastes the same as it always has. You're just in a mood.
Might be the frost got into it. Or you're finally tasting how bad it's always been.
Fixed it twice. The goat's just smarter than the fence.
I'll fix it when the goat stops needing fixing.
Fence is fine. It's the goat that needs replacing.
Working on it. Slowly. The fence isn't going anywhere.
Tired's just how I look now. Used to be pretty once, or so they tell me.
Tired's the least of what I am today. Don't get me started.
I'll sleep when the children do. So, never. Maybe I'll lie down anyway.
They probably are. I've seen the way they look at you.
Sounds about right. Ungrateful lot, chickens.
Next you'll be dreaming the goats have opinions too.
Told you not to eat cheese before bed.
That was a poor trade and you know it.
Depends how much you like turnips, I suppose. At least dinner's sorted.
The baker swears a lot of things. Mostly to sell more bread.
My back's been bad for years. If bread fixes it, that's easier than anything else I've tried.
Next he'll be selling bread that cures the taxes too.
You'd bet an emerald on anything, it’s half the reason you've none left.
Done. And when I win, you're buying the potion. I'm not walking across town for it.
Old wives' tale. Though the well has run dry twice…
Don't say that out loud. Some things are better not tempted.
Cats don't follow people. They follow whoever smells like fish.
Maybe it likes you. Or maybe it's judging you. Hard to say with cats.
Feed it once and it's yours for life, that's the rule.
That's the third this month. Bold creature.
Maybe it's time you learned to shut the coop properly.
Fox eats better than half this street, at this rate.
Set a trap or lose the rest. Your choice.
Neither have I. Something's got the dogs barking all night.
Try warm milk. Or a stiff drink. Whichever is closer.
Welcome to the club. None of us sleep well anymore.
You'd have better luck haggling with the crown.
Should've brought your wife. She'd have had him in tears.
Cursed or just deeply unpleasant? Hard to say with chickens.
Every chicken's cursed at four in the morning.
Curse it back. Can't make things worse.
Bad yeast, more like. Not every failure needs an omen.
Careful saying that too loud, some folks around here take it seriously.
If bad bread's an omen, this whole street's doomed already.
Something's got him working double time. Wonder what.
My ears haven't forgiven him for it yet. I was trying to sleep.
Or he's just terrible at fishing and won't admit it.
Give him time. He'll blame the weather before he blames himself.
Heard the shouting myself. Didn't dare look out the window.
Always something, isn't there. Never a quiet week.
Ask the weaponsmith. He's usually first to know when there's trouble.
Everything's twice what it was last month. Not just meat.
I'll go hungry before I pay that price.
Wait till the farmer's next harvest comes in. Prices always drop after.
And did you buy it?
Cracked bowl, cracked plan. Consistent, at least.
He hasn't forgotten either, trust me.
Boots that old, I'd say you've paid enough already just wearing them.
Sticks for swords and pot lids for shields. Same as we did.
Loud, but better than them under my feet in the house. Let them tire themselves out.
Let them have it while they're young. Real swords come soon enough.
Let the fletcher teach them, it keeps them out of trouble at least.
They'll lose interest in a week, same as the last thing. Saves us worrying about it now.
Better the bow than wandering off toward the smithy unsupervised.
I've a fair guess who, and I'd wager you do too.
Build a better fence or have words with them directly.
I don't need to guess, I can smell it from here.
A bold plan, but a terrible execution.
There's a lesson in there somewhere. Doubt you'll learn it though.
Good news travels slowly. Bad news arrives before breakfast.
Whatever it is, we'll hear three different versions by supper.
Must've been serious. Or everyone took too long to get to the point.
Court business. Ten people talking and one person deciding.
About the village, or about us? There's a difference.
Best start looking useful, then.
Give it a week. Someone important will ruin it.
Good. I'd rather trade with them than bury people over them.
Funny. Last season everyone swore they couldn't be trusted.
That's diplomacy for you. Today's bastard is tomorrow's dinner guest.
Someone always says that when they see a stranger in decent clothes.
If they're important enough, the herald will make sure none of us can miss it.
Should've charged them for cleaning your clothes.
At least you can say the realm's defenders are moving with purpose.
Ask me someday.
Better not let the court hear you asking questions like that.
Depends who teaches %105$s between now and then.
Your washing? Maybe they did you a favour.
Check the hedges before you accuse the whole village.
Wind's a thief too, you know.
And you've only just decided to tell everyone?
They're mine. Lost three emeralds years ago. Exactly three.
Put them back. Hidden money always belongs to someone unpleasant.
Birds.
Very clever birds.
Quick dog.
Slow hand.
Sounds fairly won to me.
Then perhaps the door simply hates you.
Hopefully nobody finds a reason to use it.
That's exactly the sort of thing I worry about you saying.
People drink when times are good and when times are bad. Must be something worse.
Maybe they're finally saving their emeralds. Or drinking at home where the chairs are better.
Then the walls already know I'm right.
Careful. That's almost treason over breakfast.
I'd settle for cheaper bread.
Put that in a petition and I'll sign it.
Probably wondering who's going to pay for it.
Rulers have different worries than us.
You could ask. I won't be standing beside you when you do.
Stones have the good sense not to get involved.
And they'll probably outlast the next few too.
Makes you wonder what they'd say if they could talk.
Most bad ideas probably did too.
Give someone a title and suddenly everyone forgets where they started.
Maybe we're standing beside the next one now.
Now I barely know everyone on my own street.
That's what happens when a village becomes a capital.
I miss the quiet more than the faces. Quiet asks less of you.
Someone ought to tell them to slow down.
Houses are cheaper to feed.
At least the children eventually stop needing new roofs.
Travelers?
Could be another family looking to stay.
Give them a week and they'll know everyone's business too.
Word gets around when a place starts growing.
More carts, more mud. That's progress, apparently.
Good for trade. Bad for sleeping. I know which one I notice first.
That's why it's always crowded.
One good gossip spot is enough if everyone talks loudly.
We need another well before we need another gossip spot.
Finally, a sensible idea.
Another well means another place for everyone to stand around talking.
We need someone to fix the first one before we start dreaming bigger.
And somehow everyone is still hungry for more.
Gossip's the only thing we never run short of.
Shame you can't bake it.
Maybe you're the one standing in everyone else's way.
That's capital life. More people, less room.
Try counting how many of them you actually like.
Wait until it rains. Then you'll complain about the mud.
I've stopped cleaning my boots. Saves the effort.
Where else would it be?
In this town? I wouldn't make assumptions.
If someone's stolen your bed, I almost respect the effort. Carrying a bed sounds exhausting.
And the guard heard it from someone's cousin, I suppose.
So nobody who actually saw it, then.
That's practically official by village standards.
Again?
Then stop beginning sentences with "I heard."
You've never once refused gossip in your life.
Sensible. Checking ruins a good story.
Then how do you know it was strange?
Then why did you tell me?
Of course not.
I make no promises.
Then I assume it's worse than it sounds.
Fine. I'll make up my own explanation.
That's only going to make me ask more questions.
Chickens know where the grain is. That's about it.
I've seen the way that one watches people.
You're spending too much time with the chickens.
That's what superstitious people always say.
Experience with what, exactly?
Fine. Be experienced somewhere farther away from me.
More organized than some people I could name.
One stared at me like I owed taxes.
Give them another week and they'll start issuing decrees.
Don't repeat that near the guards.
Depends which chicken.
I've heard worse ideas.
The chicken didn't say it, did they?
They were here first, according to them.
Try telling a chicken where it's allowed to stand.
At this point they may as well pay taxes.
